items.text: There are two ranges of iron salts containing either Fe²+ or Fe³+ ions. These reactions produce iron(Il) salts, containing Fe²+ions.

items.label: section_header
items.text: KEY POINT

items.label: text
items.text: It would be impossible to place a metal exactly in the reactivity series using this sequence. How vigorously a metal reacts with a dilute acid depends on its position in the series, but it also depends on its surface area, and whether the surface is free from dirt or an oxide coating.

items.label: text
items.text: You need to know the charge on the ion so that you can deduce the formulae of the manganese compounds. If you aren't sure about working out the formula of an ionic compound, look again at Chapter 7.

items.label: section_header
items.text: FINDING THE APPROXIMATE POSITION OF A METAL IN THE REACTIVITY SERIES USING WATER AND DILUTE ACIDS

items.label: text
items.text: Add a very small piece of metal to some cold water. If there is any rapid reaction, then the metal must be above magnesium in the reactivity series.

items.label: text
items.text: If there isn't any reaction, add a small amount of metal to some dilute hydrochloric acid (or dilute sulfuric acid). If there isn't any reaction in the cold acid, warm it carefully.

items.label: text
items.text: If there is still no reaction, the metal is probably below hydrogen in the reactivity series. If there is a reaction, then it is somewhere between magnesium and hydrogen.

items.label: section_header
items.text: MAKING PREDICTIONS USING THE REACTIVITY SERIES

items.label: text
items.text: You can make predictions about the reactions of unfamiliar metals if you know their position in the reactivity series.

items.label: text
items.text: Suppose you have a question as follows.

items.label: text
items.text: Manganese (Mn) lies between aluminium and zinc in the reactivity series, and forms a 2+ ion. Solutions of manganese(ll) salts are very pale pink (almost colourless).

items.label: list_item
items.text: a Use the reactivity series to predict whether manganese will react with copper(ll) sulfate solution. If it will react, describe what you would see, name the products and write an equation for the reaction.

items.label: list_item
items.text: b Explain why you would expect manganese to react with steam. Name the products of the reaction and write the equation.
